taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes American ranid genus arrangements are contested (Lithobates vs Rana); the batch name follows NatureServe's Lithobates. NatureServe's English name is North American Bullfrog.
fieldMarks: Green or brown, usually with dark spots or mottling, not large rounded spots
No ridges along each side of the back; large eardrum with a skin fold curving around it
Males: eardrum distinctly larger than the eye, yellow throat in breeding season, swollen thumb base
Up to about 20 cm snout-vent; 4th hind toe extends past the webbing
behavior: Breeding call is a deep bellowing 'um-rum'
Movements and breeding mostly at dusk and at night, though it calls by day too
Larvae usually overwinter at least once in the north
Eats any animal it can swallow
habitat: Ponds, swamps, lakes, marshes and ditches with floating or emergent vegetation.
range: Native from Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and southern Québec west to the Great Lakes and south through most of the central and eastern US to northeastern Mexico; widely introduced in the west.

lookalikes.name: Green frog
lookalikes.howToTell: Has a ridge along each side of the back and a banjo-string call; bullfrogs have no such ridges.
